top_changes.change: Replace the dashed-lane current markings with flowing foam/ripple bands that follow the water (scrolling normal-map streaks, foam trails, debris drift), and give restoration a visible calm-water/sandbar/colour payoff
Build Veilfall as the board's tiered, vegetated monumental mountain with multiple layered falls, base spray and arched entrance, readable from First Shore

Rework shiny materials to a hue-shifted palette that preserves species pattern (no flat magenta), and author distinct swim/hurt/moving/faint/rest poses plus grounded volumetric telegraphs instead of flat pink rings

rows.reason: Islands now read as pale dune sand with sparse beach-grass clumps and some shrub/tree pockets, matching the dunes ruling; but dunes are smooth untextured mounds with uniform sand colour, no wet dark shore band or salt rock layering, and offshore islets are identical flat sand ovals.

Moving frames for Ripplet, Mosshell, Cragclaw, Torrentoad and Riptusk are near-identical to idle; hurt reads only slightly (Riverdrake, Mangrove Monitor lean) while Mosshell/Cannonback hurt keep the idle silhouette.
Map canvas is a black rectangle with one octagonal marker and no terrain, coastline, islands or route context; 'Surveyed 0%' leaves it unusable as a picture.

Abyssal Guardian, Cragclaw, Mangrove Monitor, Riverdrake, Sirenseal and Torrentoad shinies are flat saturated hot magenta that erase pattern and material; only Mosshell, Cannonback, Tidecoil and Riptusk keep a species-legible palette shift.
No ground pickups are shown in any frame.

Veilfall is a dark blocky rock tower with a single thin white streak from distance and a flat white-quad cascade beside a dark faceted cliff close up; nothing approaches the board's tiered, green-capped, multi-fall monument with arch and spray.
Visible destinations are bare sand ovals with a single tree or small prop; only a lone timber beacon and a stone ring gate appear, with no distinct hall, arch or terrace silhouettes.

Arms are now raised, but the trainer is still bolt-upright with both hands straight overhead and boots/legs visible below the surface; it reads as a stand-up wave or 'help' gesture, not a horizontal swim stroke.

Aquaryn, Riptusk, Torrentoad, Sirenseal and Riverdrake now lie collapsed; Ripplet still sits upright with head raised as in idle and Tidecoil keeps a lifted head curve, so the defeat read is inconsistent.
Menus are now translucent blue-grey over the live world with tabs, cards and a creature portrait, giving some hierarchy; still small type, uniform panel weight and no illustrated or biome flavour.
Build now has three illustrated cards and Save has slot rows, but Quests and Players remain mostly empty dark space around a handful of small text lines.
Only a few NPCs appear; they share the same chunky low-detail body and similar brown palettes, and nothing here demonstrates distinct named-role silhouettes.
Water now shows a clear turquoise-shallow to navy-deep gradient with foam halos around sandbars and sun glitter; distance haze and depth variation offshore are still fairly uniform.

Tells are still thin flat pink/magenta ground ellipses plus text banners ('incoming — move', 'HEAVY — get clear'); hit frames show a faint pink beam with almost no impact flash or recoil silhouette on Cannonback.
No catch frames included.
The supplied fight is Ripplet vs Cannonback; no Riverdrake fight frames.
Exploration HUD is reduced to a team card, story box, minimap, hotbar and prompt strip around the edges; still several separate dark boxes but the centre view is clear.
A pale foam ring now surrounds the swimmer, but it is a uniform flat disc with no trailing wake or splash, and the legs are visible beneath giving no displaced-water read.
No candy pickups shown.
The left team roster now sits on a dark backing with teal bars and stays readable over grass and sand, though icons and text are tiny at 1280-class raster.
No partially buried blue figure is visible behind Ripplet across the Venn fight frames; only the trainer stands on the sand.
A straight receding chain of near-identical tan sand ovals with white foam rims runs to the horizon, reading as mechanical stepping stones rather than natural shoals.

Bindings are now laid out in gamepad/keyboard columns with section headers, but text is small grey on navy, uses literal 'Left stick up'/'D-pad left' strings with no glyphs, and the map help line is a dense key list.
Live currents are bright white dashed lane lines with chevron arrows on a flat lighter strip, literally road markings painted on the sea; t0/t1 are nearly identical.
Restored state only dims the dashed lines (still visible) and removes the lighter strip; sandbars, water colour, foam and surroundings are unchanged, so restoration has no environmental payoff.
No dialogue frames included.
